'''Michael Porter Jr.''' (born June 29, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball at the [[University of Missouri]]. Porter was ranked as one of the top prospects in the class of 2017. He is regarded as one of the top prospects in the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref name="247 sports">{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Michael-Porter-34291|title=Michael Porter, Nathan Hale , Small Forward|website=247Sports}}</ref><ref name="espn.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/193628/michael-porter-jr|title=Michael Porter Jr. - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref name="rivals.com">{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/373|title=Rivals.com|website=n.rivals.com}}</ref>

==High school career==
Porter attended [[Father Tolton Regional Catholic High School]] in [[Columbia, Missouri]], before transferring to [[Nathan Hale High School]] in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]], for his senior year. His father, Michael Porter Sr., was hired by the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|University of Washington]] to be an assistant coach; former NBA star [[Brandon Roy]] was the coach of Nathan Hale's basketball team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/michael-porter-jr-brother-transfer-to-nathan-hale-seattle-to-play-for-new-coach-brandon-roy|title=Michael Porter Jr., Jontay transfer to Nathan Hale (Seattle) to play for new coach Brandon Roy|date=25 June 2016|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.columbiatribune.com/sports/prep_sports/tolton/michael-and-jontay-porter-leaving-storied-high-school-careers-with/article_55b08978-034b-5b41-9b93-0dfdca56df1d.html|title=Michael and Jontay Porter leaving storied high school careers with move to Seattle|first=Daniel Jones dmjones@columbiatribune.com ||last=815-1787|publisher=}}</ref> In his senior season, he would average a massive 36.2 points and 13.6 rebounds as he helped the high school earn a perfect 29–0 record and win the Washington Class 3A State Championship. Porter was rated as a five-star recruit and ranked as one of the top overall recruits in his class by [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].<ref name="rivals.com"/><ref name="espn.com"/>

He participated in the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], leading Team USA to a 98–87 victory over the World Select Team with 19 points in 23 minutes of play.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|title=LiveStats - USA vs World Select Team - Nike Hoop Summit|access-date=2017-04-08|language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
In July 2016, Porter originally committed to [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/17085923/top-recruit-michael-porter-jr-commits-play-washington-huskies|title=Top recruit Porter commits to play at Washington|publisher=}}</ref> After [[Lorenzo Romar]] was fired as Washington's head coach, Porter Sr. was hired as an assistant coach for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|University of Missouri]]. Porter Jr. later decommitted from Washington.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article89974157.html|title=Top basketball recruit Michael Porter Jr. commits to Washington instead of MU, other finalists|publisher=}}</ref>

On March 24, 2017, Porter committed to play for Missouri, joining his father and his younger brother, [[Jontay Porter]] (who reclassified from the class of 2018).

Porter was injured in the first half of the season opener against Iowa State. Porter was expected to miss the remainder of the 2017–18 season because of a lower back injury which required surgery.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21505145/missouri-freshman-forward-michael-porter-jr-likely-miss-remainder-season|title=Michael Porter Jr. to have back surgery, likely out for rest of season|publisher=espn.com|author=ESPN Newswire|date=2017-11-21|accessdate=2017-11-21}}</ref> On November 22, 2017, Porter had a successful microdiscectomy of his L3-L4 spinal discs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Porter Jr. Has Surgery|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/no-slam-dunk-michael-porters-back-surgery-plants-doubt-into-2018-nba-draft/|website=CBS Sports|publisher=CBS}}</ref> However, on February 22, 2018, Porter Jr. was cleared to practice with Missouri again, with the potential to return to play before the end of the season. [[NBA]] executives are encouraging him to play if he's feeling healthy enough to do so.<ref>https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/missouri-freshman-michael-porter-jr-cleared-for-all-basketball-activities/</ref> Porter would officially return to action on March 8, 2018 in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|SEC Tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22694904/michael-porter-jr-not-especially-sharp-return-missouri-tigers|title=Michael Porter Jr. off in return from back surgery|publisher=espn.com|author=Alex Scarborough|date=2018-03-08|accessdate=2018-03-08}}</ref> Porter would also play in the first round of the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]], where the team lost to [[2017–18 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. In both games, however, Porter would be coming off of the bench to play instead of being named a starter like he was on opening night, mainly as a precaution. On March 27, Porter announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he is expected to be a [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] selection.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Kyle |last=Boone|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2018-nba-draft-michael-porter-jr-declares-after-one-injury-plagued-year-at-missouri/|title=2018 NBA Draft: Michael Porter Jr. declares after one injury-plagued year at Missouri|work=cbssports.com.com|access-date= March 27, 2018|date=March 27, 2018}}</ref>
